title: Domain decomposition, an MPI solver, and performance analysis
status: reviewed and locally validated; independent round 2 ACCEPT
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: All three assigned machine transcripts were read completely and the 25 listed frames inspected. No complete independent audio review was performed. Public corrections about Jacobi, send ordering and Karp–Flatt are supported by viewed slides/code rather than garbled speech.

The chapter changes the lecture heat boundaries, precision, hard-coded process count and unsafe exchange to the canonical top-one double-precision model with configurable strips/tiles. The lecture temperature trace and approximately 2.61-second example are not local reproduction targets.
METIS was not installed or executed. The graph listing checks CSR and explicit candidate partitions; it neither runs the package nor proves global partition optimality.

Gustafson 1988 was opened through a university-hosted primary-paper copy with three PDF pages and a typographic 1088 footer. The bibliographic year 1988 and CACM volume 31 issue 5 are distinguished from that footer. The original Amdahl 1967 paper was not independently opened; the chapter reconstructs the fixed-size bound and relies on Gustafson for its contrast and attribution.

Karp and Flatt 1990 was opened as a five-page scan hosted by a parallel-computing course/repository. The metric derivation and discussion on printed pages 539–540 were read. No unique causal-identification claim is inferred from its examples.
MPI 4.1 is the normative reference, while the installed library reports MPI 3.1. All listed routines predate MPI 4.1; this is not an exhaustive comparison of wording across editions.

Four timing captures were serialized in an exclusive agent slot, using TCP loopback plus self transport and no binding. OS services, CPU frequency and migration on the hybrid CPU remained uncontrolled. These are neither shared-memory-transport nor inter-node measurements.

Serial reference timing in multi-rank jobs occurs while peers wait at a barrier and can consume CPU progress resources; serial_over_mpi is not an isolated serial-process benchmark. Strong-scaling ratios consistently use the one-rank MPI kernel in the same capture.

Weak scaling has only two process counts, holds cells per rank and sweep count fixed, and does not establish time-to-solution scaling for a converged finer-grid solve. Fixed update tolerance does not enforce a fixed PDE residual threshold across N.

The surface model uses explicitly hypothetical coefficients, bidirectional per-face costs, serialized faces, interior ranks and no contention. The isoefficiency extension is original teaching material, not presented as developed lecture content. No empirical protocol crossover is inferred.
Open MPI emitted debugger_attach_fifo errno 95 on the Windows-mounted workspace. Raw stderr is retained. All numerical jobs exited 0, but debugger attachment was not tested or claimed supported.

The final structured checker reran the complete listing once after the reported four captures. Its variable timing output is functional verification evidence and is not included in the four-capture ranges.

A pre-review local-PDF citation audit corrected the null-process reference from §3.11 to the actual official-PDF §3.10 (printed p.111). Collective Chapter 6, Cartesian Chapter 8 and all audited printed page references were confirmed directly against the local official PDF; executable listing and output contracts were unchanged.
lecture_corrections: The displayed heat update reads told and writes t using four-neighbour averaging: Jacobi, not a general SOR recurrence.
Blocking sends before receives can depend on standard-mode buffering; an end barrier cannot repair that deadlock risk. The safe implementation uses Sendrecv or posted requests.
A barrier every sweep is not independently necessary once data dependencies and common stopping decisions are established by the implemented exchanges and Allreduce.
Karp–Flatt inversion gives e=f+kappa/[T1(1−1/p)], not generally (sigma+kappa)/(sigma+phi). Both conflicting slide definitions were inspected.
Constant effective serial fraction is consistent with genuine serial work but does not uniquely establish it; an overhead-only model reproduces the curve.
Rounded lecture speedups give approximately constant 0.1 in table 1, not exactly 0.1 at every printed point.
An unstructured face-adjacent tetrahedral dual graph has at most four neighbours per tetrahedron; this does not extend to every mesh-derived graph.
